Package it.polimi.ingsoft.mesos.client.view.gui

package it.polimi.ingsoft.mesos.client.view.gui
JavaFX Graphical User Interface (GUI) for the Mesos client.

What lives in this package

  • GUIView — the single JavaFX controller. It implements ClientView (the input side: payloads coming from the server are rendered into nodes) and at the same time owns the @FXML-injected fields and @FXML event handlers referenced by gui.fxml (the output side: user interactions are translated into commands sent through a ServerProxy).
  • gui.fxml (sibling resources folder) — the only FXML file of the application. It declares the static layout: a BorderPane shell with a top bar and a centred StackPane fx:id="pages" that contains five sibling pages (login, lobby list, lobby form, game, end). Exactly one page is made visible at a time by showPage(Node).
  • mesos-gui.css (sibling resources folder) — visual theme applied to the scene. FXML nodes are themed through their styleClass attribute, which maps directly to CSS class selectors (e.g. styleClass="primary-button" ↔ .primary-button { ... }).

How FXML binds to GUIView

The binding between gui.fxml and GUIView relies on three naming conventions that are enforced at FXML load time:

  1. fx:id="foo" on an FXML node injects that node into the @FXML private SomeType foo field of the controller. The field name and the node type must match exactly.
  2. onAction="#handleFoo" on an FXML control calls the @FXML private void handleFoo() method of the controller. The method must be void and take either zero arguments or a single ActionEvent.
  3. styleClass="bar" on an FXML node binds it to the .bar selector in mesos-gui.css. JavaFX CSS uses the -fx-... property prefix (e.g. -fx-background-color).

The annotated @FXML private void initialize() method runs automatically after FXML injection completes; it is the place to seed combo-boxes, choose the initial page, and start auxiliary timers.

Threading model

JavaFX nodes can only be read or modified on the JavaFX Application Thread. GUIView receives server payloads from TCP and RMI networking threads, so every ClientView callback delegates its UI work through runOnFx(Runnable), which runs the work immediately when already on the FX thread and otherwise schedules it through Platform.runLater(java.lang.Runnable). @FXML event handlers, by contrast, are already invoked on the FX thread and must not be wrapped again.

Page-stack architecture

All five logical screens of the application live as sibling children of the central StackPane. They are not separate FXML files. Pages therefore share the same scene graph and the same controller, and dynamic content (lobby cards, market cards, offer-path tiles, player rows, tribe strips, final ranking) is rendered into empty placeholder containers such as lobbyListContainer, upperRowContainer, lowerRowContainer, offerPathContainer, playerListContainer, tribeCardsContainer and finalRankingContainer.

Where to go next

For a step-by-step modification guide (adding a button, adding a page, binding a new payload to the UI, recipes and common pitfalls) see the Markdown document assets/guides/guide-javafx-gui-modification.md in the project root.
